prTitle: Improve time complexity and reduce memory allocations

content.motivation: The goal of this change is to optimize the tool definition resolution process in DefaultToolCallingManager by replacing an O(N*M) nested loop (stream.anyMatch inside a loop) with an O(N+M) approach using a HashSet lookup, improving performance during tool name validation.
goodPoints: Performance improvement achieved by reducing algorithmic complexity for checking duplicate tool names.
Logic is functionally equivalent to the original implementation.
Correctly handles potential null or empty collections by leveraging the Set API.
badPoints: Usage of wildcard imports (java.util.*) degrades code readability and violates clean code practices regarding explicit imports.
Static analysis issues (PMD/Checkstyle) present in the file were not cleaned up while modifying the area.
Failure to remove previously used individual imports after migrating to a wildcard import.
content.suggestion: Replace the wildcard import 'java.util.*' with explicit imports for the classes actually used (e.g., Set, HashSet, Collectors). Additionally, address the existing PMD warnings (specifically the logger naming convention, guard log statements, and modifier ordering) to improve overall code quality in the file.

details: Replaced the stream-based 'anyMatch' check with a Set-based 'contains' check for O(1) lookups.
Created 'existingToolNames' set from 'chatOptions.getToolCallbacks()' to pre-calculate tool availability.
Maintained existing tool ordering by iterating over 'chatOptions.getToolNames()' and checking against the populated Set.
